title: Critical and multicritical Kasner scaling in holographic phase transitions
authors: Ling-Long Gao, Yan Liu, Hong-Da Lyu
abstract: We study how holographic phase transitions imprint their scaling laws on the local Kasner geometry inside Einstein-scalar black holes. At fixed double-trace coupling, we derive the near-critical scaling of the deviation of the first-epoch Kasner exponent from the Schwarzschild value: $p_t^{(1)}+\frac{1}{3} \propto O^2 \propto (T_c-T)^{1/r}$, where $O$ denotes the boundary condensate and $r$ labels ordinary criticality ($r=1$), tricriticality ($r=2$), and higher multicriticality ($r\geq3$). A super-exponential scalar potential generates a sequence of Kasner epochs separated by scalar-field bounces. We further find that any later epoch that can be tracked continuously across the transition inherits the same temperature exponent, while its coefficient depends on the epoch. Numerical solutions confirm these predictions for the ordinary and tricritical cases. Finally, we show analytically that the leading irrelevant exponent of the infrared fixed point governs the low-temperature Kasner scaling, and verify the resulting scaling numerically for the first Kasner exponent.
summary: This paper analyzes how holographic phase transitions dictate the scaling laws observed in the anisotropic Kasner geometry inside black holes. It derives specific power-law scalings for the deviation of the Kasner exponents near criticality, showing that these patterns persist across multiple interior epochs. The work connects boundary critical phenomena to the deep spacetime structure via advanced gravitational and thermodynamic techniques.
main_problem: The study investigates how holographic phase transitions imprint their scaling laws onto the local Kasner geometry within Einstein-scalar black holes.
main_result: The deviation of the first-epoch Kasner exponent scales according to a power law dependent on the critical order ($r$), and later epochs inherit the same temperature exponent as the initial one.
method: The analysis employs perturbative methods, scaling symmetries, and Infrared (IR) matching techniques to connect boundary critical behavior to the black hole interior dynamics.
model_or_system: The system is a 4D Einstein-scalar gravity model dual to a boundary field theory deformed by a double-trace operator. The geometry involves hairy black holes whose interiors are analyzed using Kasner-like solutions.
key_observables: Kasner exponents ($p_t, p_x, p_\phi$), the boundary condensate ($\alpha$), and the renormalized free energy density ($F$).
important_parameters: The critical order $r$ (ordinary $r=1$, tricritical $r=2$, etc.), temperature deviation $(T_c-T)$, and the leading irrelevant exponent of the IR fixed point.
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on super-exponential scalar potentials, and certain results rely on assuming only decreasing transitions exist in the interior evolution.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the sequence of infinitely many Kasner epochs separated by bounces inside the black hole, and one figure shows a special hairy solution exhibiting a Schwarzschild-like interior despite exterior hair.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the general framework using planar ansatz solutions to deriving scaling laws for the first epoch. It then analyzes sequences of subsequent epochs, connects low-temperature behavior to IR fixed points, and finally discusses screening mechanisms that can revert the interior dynamics to a simple Schwarzschild form.
why_interesting: While primarily in gravity/QFT, the study of phase transitions (criticality, multicriticality) and the connection between bulk geometry and boundary thermodynamics is highly relevant to understanding critical phenomena in strongly coupled quantum systems.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

figures.caption: Figure 1: A typical interior evolution of a hairy black brane solution in Einstein-scalar the- ory with super-exponent potential (2.2). Here ρ = log(z/zh). Kasner epochs correspond to the plateau regime in the left panel and the sloped regime in the right panel, while bounces correspond to the jumps between two epochs in both panels.

Figure 2: Thermodynamics and condensate at the generic second-order critical point at λ4 = λ = λ8 = 1/10, λ6 = 0. Left: free-energy densities of the Schwarzschild (gray) and hairy (blue) black holes. Right: The order parameter O/(−κ) as a function of T/(−κ). In both panels, the black dot marks the critical point of the phase transition, while the red dot denotes the corresponding zero-temperature domain wall solution. The insets are log-log plots: ∆F versus ∆T = Tc −T on the left, and O versus ∆T on the right. We work in unit κ = −1.

Figure 3: The Kasner exponent pt as a function of the temperature T (left) and condensate O (right) for λ4 = λ = λ8 = 1/10, λ6 = 0. In the left plot, the gray line is the Schwarzschild value pt = −1/3; the first (blue), second (red), and third (green) epochs are shown separately, while the polynomial model without the super-exponential term (i.e. set λ = 0) (black dashed) is included for comparison. Interestingly, pt ≃pSch t at a special temperature T = 0.11965, as shown in the inset of the left panel, and interior of the hairy black hole becomes Schwarzschild-like, details of the interior are discussed in Appendix D. We work in unit κ = −1.

Figure 4: The first three continuously tracked Kasner epochs in the ordinary critical phase transition for λ4 = λ = λ8 = 1/10, λ6 = 0. Left: ∆p(n) t versus ∆T; Right: ∆p(n) t versus O. In both panels different colors denote different epochs: n = 1 (blue), 2 (red), 3 (green). All epochs have the predicted critical powers.

Figure 5: Log-log plot of ∆pt = p(1) t −pSch t at extremely low-temperature of the super- exponential model with λ4 = λ = λ8 = 1/10, λ6 = 0 (left), and polynomial model with λ = 0, λ4 = 1/10 and λ6 = 0 (right). The black dots are numerical data, while the blue lines are the fitting. In both models, the numerical fitted amplitude and exponent agree with the analytic values to the first three significant digits.
